title: A Locker for the Playlist
premise: Mara Oyelaran has survived being the only out kid in Halverson, Nebraska, by keeping her head down and her real self locked in a shared playlist with her best friend Dee — songs that say everything they can't. When a college essay prompt asks students to write about 'a truth you've kept,' Mara writes honestly about Dee's older brother, who died by suicide two years ago and whose death the town buried in silence. The essay wins a scholarship contest and is read aloud at assembly, detonating the town's careful forgetting and exposing how Dee's family has been drowning ever since. Mara must choose between retracting the truth to save the friendship or standing in it as graduation — and Dee's own breaking point — arrive; she keeps the truth, loses Dee temporarily, and finds her again at the edge of leaving, both of them finally saying out loud what the playlist always said.
about_author: Emrys Almeida is the pen name of a former small-town debate coach who grew up in a farming community of fewer than a thousand people and never quite left it on paper. They write quiet, music-soaked stories about kids who learn that telling the truth is a kind of survival skill.

chapters.title: Track One: Static
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A ordinary October morning in Halverson establishes Mara's countdown calendar, her mother's diner shifts, and the shared Spotify playlist — 214 songs — that she and Dee have built since seventh grade. Emotional beat: suffocating tenderness; Mara loves this town the way you love a room you can't leave.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. English teacher Mr. Brandt assigns the scholarship essay: 'Write about a truth you've kept.' That night Mara drafts three safe versions about her grandmother's recipes before accidentally writing one true sentence about Theo, Dee's brother, dead two years and barely mentioned since. Beat: the shock of honesty arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: Two Hundred and Fourteen Songs
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. We see the friendship from inside Dee: the playlist is their language, and Theo's absence hums under every track. Dee notices Mara acting strange but assumes it's college stress. Beat: dramatic irony and ache — the reader sees the collision coming before either girl does.

chapters.title: What the Town Agreed Not to Say
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Researching the essay, Mara interviews the pastor, the football coach, and Theo's old girlfriend, discovering everyone knew Theo was struggling and no one said so. She finishes the essay at 2 a.m., hands shaking. Beat: dread hardening into resolve; the truth has weight now.

chapters.title: Submission
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Mara submits without telling Dee; Dee learns of the contest entry from a guidance-counselor email and confronts Mara in the locker bay where they always meet. First real fight in six years. Beat: betrayal felt from both sides — Mara's secrecy, Dee's silence.

chapters.title: Assembly
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The essay wins; the principal reads it aloud to nine hundred people. Halfway through, Dee walks out. By evening the town is split between gratitude and fury, and Dee's mother stops speaking to Mara's family at the diner. Beat: public detonation; no way back.

chapters.title: Locker Bay, Empty
chapters.summary: Dee's POV. Weeks of silence. Dee rereads the playlist and realizes Mara wrote about Theo because she loved him too, not to exploit him. But pride and grief keep Dee locked. Meanwhile Mara throws herself into scholarship paperwork like penance. Beat: grief misdirected as anger; loneliness on both sides of the lockers.

chapters.title: The Voicemail
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Dee's father, drunk and desperate, leaves Mara a voicemail thanking her — the family's insurance ran out, and strangers have quietly sent help since the essay published. Mara plays it for Dee outside her house in the snow. Beat: the price of survival reframed; truth as inheritance, not theft.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Caps, gowns, and a gymnasium of everyone who took sides. Dee gives the student address and abandons her prepared speech to read the last song title on the playlist aloud — track 215, which she added the night after the assembly: an apology in three minutes of chords. Beat: climax; the private language spoken publicly at last.

chapters.title: Track Two Hundred Fifteen
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. After graduation, the girls sit in the locker bay one final time before Mara leaves for Chicago. They talk about Theo plainly, out loud, for the first time. Dee decides to stay a year and get the town's mental-health fund off the ground; Mara goes, but the playlist stays synced. Beat: bittersweet resolution — truth cost them everything except each other.
